conclusions: Repeated positively speech-supported words constrain boundary searches more narrowly than cue-start anchors alone. Three contiguous exact words retain the production lexical score gate of 0.35; this is not a replacement for the six-word/0.7 absent-dialogue gate.

The initial crossing after-flank pair is unavailable. One additional fixed 15-second decode starting at 66 seconds provides matching words across the two later windows. The initial failure is retained.

With those word constraints and the production native converter, top spectral-tilt boundary errors are 0.14 seconds for the crossing-cue insertion and 0.68 seconds for the other insertion. Energy alone still fails the latter at 1.61 seconds.
Replacing word flanks with only the existing accepted cue starts produces a wrong spectral-tilt candidate, 4.91 seconds from the second insertion. Cue clusters alone are insufficient.
limitations: Two consumed development fixtures with hard edits; no held-out or crossfade validation.
Feature selection and confidence/ambiguity rejection are not calibrated. These rankings are proposals, not confirmed gaps.
The richer word evidence currently comes from bounded offline re-decodes; its reliable availability in the live pipeline is unproven.
The proposal is available after post-edit matches. No early suppression or first-playback recovery improvement is demonstrated.
A production implementation would need bounded retained feature metadata after PCM eviction; no audio may be retained for later full-episode reanalysis.
